newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat drops to 22 pct very poor to poor.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat drops to 22 pct very poor to poor.

text.p: Twenty-two percent of the Kansas wheat crop dropped into the poor to very poor category during the week ended Sunday, compared with nine percent the previous week, according to the Kansas Agricultural Statistical Reporting Service.

Freezing temperatures the weekend of April 12-13 harmed the crop, with the reporting service pegging the freeze damage at 14 percent severe, 26 percent moderate, 24 percent light and 36 percent with no damage.
Wheat in the northern part of the state was less developed and under snow cover. It appears to not have received damage as extensive as southern areas.
As of April 20, wheat condition was rated three percent excellent, 37 percent good, 38 percent fair, 17 percent poor and five percent very poor.
Pasture conditions for the state were rated five percent poor, 27 percent fair, 61 percent good and seven percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture levels were one percent very short, eight percent short, 80 percent adequate and 11 percent surplus.
